gaps.sentence: The ambush ___ (plan) by someone with intimate knowledge of the valley.
gaps.explanation: Past perfect passive (had been planned) stresses completion before the ambush; was planned is also acceptable.

gaps.sentence: The temple is thought ___ (build) more than two thousand years ago.
gaps.explanation: Perfect passive infinitive: to have been + built for an event earlier than the main verb.

gaps.sentence: The office ___ (repaint) at the moment, so we're working from home.
gaps.explanation: Present continuous passive: am/is/are being + past participle. 'At the moment' signals it.

gaps.sentence: She had her laptop ___ (repair) after the coffee spill.
gaps.explanation: Causative structure: had + her laptop + repaired. A technician performed the repair.

gaps.sentence: The manuscript is said ___ in a private vault for decades.
gaps.explanation: 'For decades' before now: perfect passive infinitive to have been + kept.

gaps.sentence: Endangered plants ___ (not pick) anywhere in the reserve.
gaps.explanation: Modal passive of prohibition: must not be + past participle.

gaps.sentence: We had the whole house ___ (repaint) before the wedding.
gaps.explanation: 'Had the house repainted' — painters did it at our request. Object + past participle.

gaps.sentence: Your luggage ___ (weigh) at check-in, so allow extra time.
gaps.explanation: Future simple passive: will be + weighed. The agent (staff) is obvious.
